findings.title: Findings converge on the Compatibility posture's upgrade path
findings.why_it_matters: Three findings, raised by both critics from different angles, each patch what an existing user hits on the first start after upgrading: a hard `ConfigError` from a removed `autodetect`/`exclude_dirs` key (Finding 3), a database an older image refuses to open after a rollback (Finding 8), and apps built on a shared base class that silently stop running with no warning (Finding 9). Each proposes its own footer line or code. The common cause is that D1-D10 are all framed around the newcomer, and Posture's Compatibility line says only that the change "breaks freely" with "one `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer", not what an upgrader actually sees. Should the upgrade path be re-evaluated as one question (which consequences are accepted limitations, which deserve a change, where the guidance lives), rather than settled as three separate footer fragments?
findings.recommended: A: Re-evaluate the Compatibility posture's upgrade path before addressing Findings 3, 8, 9 individually. Open questions the re-evaluation must answer: what does each kind of existing user (relied on autodetect; set `autodetect = false`; set `exclude_dirs` or the env vars; has a base-class hierarchy; rolls back) see on first start? Which of those are accepted limitations and which deserve a change? Where is upgrade guidance recorded, and does the ledger need a decision for it?
findings.chosen: A: Re-evaluate the Compatibility posture's upgrade path before addressing Findings 3, 8, 9 individually.

findings.title: The add-on's seeded first run depends on autodetect, and the seed files are out of scope
findings.why_it_matters: The add-on seeds an empty config with `apps/example_app.py` and a `hassette.toml` whose header says "Apps in the apps folder next to this file are found and started without any entry here", with the `[hassette.apps.example_app]` entry commented out. After this change, the seeded example never runs on a fresh install, the header comment is false, and the add-on docs page says the same false thing. This is the newcomer audience the design is written for, hit on first launch by the project's own shipped files. The design's docs list names the Docker docs, examples, and demo apps, but not `docker/addon/seed/` or the add-on configuration page.
findings.recommended: A: Add `docker/addon/seed/hassette.toml`, `docker/addon/seed/apps/example_app.py`, and `docs/pages/getting-started/addon/configuration.md` to the Assumed docs list, ship the seed with `[hassette.apps.example_app]` uncommented, and rewrite the seed header and docs line to say each app needs an entry.
findings.chosen: A: Add `docker/addon/seed/hassette.toml`, `docker/addon/seed/apps/example_app.py`, and `docs/pages/getting-started/addon/configuration.md` to the Assumed docs list, ship the seed with `[hassette.apps.example_app]` uncommented, and rewrite the seed header and docs line to say each app needs an entry.

findings.title: Upgrading with `autodetect` or `exclude_dirs` set is a hard startup failure with no actionable message
findings.why_it_matters: Once both fields leave `AppsConfig`, spec 128's unknown-key check turns an existing scalar `autodetect = false` or list `exclude_dirs = [...]` under `[hassette.apps]` into a startup `ConfigError`, since only dict-valued keys there are skipped as app definitions. `HASSETTE__APPS__AUTODETECT` / `HASSETTE__APPS__EXCLUDE_DIRS` fail the same way through `EnvNames`. The message is the generic "Unknown configuration keys ... did you mean ...?", and difflib won't map `autodetect` to anything useful. The users hit hardest are the ones who set `autodetect = false` (the repo's own `examples/hassette.toml`, `scripts/demo_apps/hassette.toml`, and test configs do), who already had the new behavior and now can't start: in Docker, that is a restart loop after an image bump.
findings.recommended: A: State in Posture that the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer names `apps.autodetect`, `apps.exclude_dirs`, `HASSETTE__APPS__AUTODETECT`, and `HASSETTE__APPS__EXCLUDE_DIRS` and says to delete them, and add `test_unknown_keys` cases for both keys alongside the existing `removed-apps-key` case.

findings.title: D5 names the wrong compat ignore file and leaves the schema-version question unrecorded
findings.why_it_matters: D5 and Posture name only `tools/client_compat_ignore.txt`, which covers fixture parsing by the released client (`nox -s client_compat`). The oasdiff gate `tools/check_wire_compat.py` is a separate check that blocks on every ERR-level finding, and removing the required `auto_loaded` response property from `AppManifestInfo` is ERR. Its own ignore file, `tools/wire_compat_ignore.txt`, is where a deliberate break adds one line per finding. The build checklist as written sends the builder to the wrong file first. Separately, the `MIN_API_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump rule only fires when the client newly depends on server API; removing a field the client required adds no dependency, so no bump is due. Writing that down keeps `tools/check_client_floor.py` from being a surprise.
findings.chosen: In Posture's Compatibility line and D5, name both `tools/wire_compat_ignore.txt` (oasdiff findings for the removed `auto_loaded` property) and `tools/client_compat_ignore.txt` (released-client fixture failures), and add one sentence to D5: no `API_SCHEMA_VERSION`/`MIN_API_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump, because removing a required field adds no server dependency under the rule in `client/src/hassette_client/version.py`. Add the same pointer to the `hassette_wire.apps` bullet in Assumed.

findings.title: The test, tooling, and script blast radius is not enumerated
findings.why_it_matters: Assumed checks only the harness. Several system tests rely on autodetect as the way apps get loaded, a unit test patches `hassette.config.config.autodetect_apps` (which disappears), and seed, tooling, mock, and frontend fixture files carry `auto_loaded`. Most of these fail loudly, so the cost is build-time churn rather than a bug, but "one session builds it" is optimistic without the list. One file must not be edited: the frozen release spec fixture.
findings.chosen: Add an Assumed bullet listing the files above as build-time updates: system tests that relied on discovery get explicit `[hassette.apps.*]` manifests; `{"autodetect": False}` test dicts are deleted; the `autodetect_apps` unit tests are deleted or rewritten for the scan; seed, tooling, mock, and frontend fixtures drop `auto_loaded` (including the "seven keyword arguments" count in `tools/client_compat_live_state.py`); `classes.py:215`'s `display_name` default loses its `auto_loaded` branch. State that `tests/unit/tools/fixtures/client_floor/v0.55.0-openapi.json` is a frozen release spec and stays unchanged.

findings.title: The paste-ready snippet breaks for apps in subdirectories and for non-module-level classes
findings.why_it_matters: D9's whole value is a snippet that works when pasted. The old code built manifests with `filename=py_file.name`, dropping the subdirectory; if the new warning copies that, a class in `apps/lights/foo.py` yields `filename = "foo.py"`, which fails with file-not-found once pasted. `clean_app` joins `app_dir / filename`, so a relative posix path with directories is accepted and is the correct value. Separately, `ast.walk` also finds classes nested in functions or under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, but the loader resolves `class_name` as a module attribute, so a snippet for such a class can never load.
findings.chosen: In D9, state that the snippet's `filename` is the file's path relative to `apps.directory` as posix (both sides resolved before `relative_to`), and in D2 that only module top-level class definitions (`tree.body`) count. Add a build test with an app in a subdirectory whose snippet, pasted as config, loads.

findings.title: The external hassette-addon repo's shipped config is unchecked for the removed keys
findings.why_it_matters: `bump-addon` commits version bumps to `NodeJSmith/hassette-addon` on every release. If that repo's default `hassette.toml`, options schema, or env setup sets `autodetect`, `exclude_dirs`, or their env vars, the first add-on release after this change fails at startup for every add-on user through Finding 3's unknown-key path. This repo's `docker/` has no references to either key, but the add-on repo wasn't inspected, so this is an unverified edge, not a confirmed bug.
findings.chosen: Add an Assumed bullet (or a Build item): before merge, grep `NodeJSmith/hassette-addon` for `autodetect`, `exclude_dirs`, `HASSETTE__APPS__AUTODETECT`, and `HASSETTE__APPS__EXCLUDE_DIRS`, and remove any hit there before this release ships.

findings.title: Dropping the `auto_loaded` column blocks rollback to an older image
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: solo or small user base on pinned Docker tags; the cost is a manual DB delete on rollback and it is not data-corrupting. `014.sql` moves `PRAGMA user_version` to 14, and an older binary refuses to open a DB that is ahead of its head ("Refusing to auto-delete — upgrade the binary or remove the database manually"). Left in place, the column costs nothing: it has `DEFAULT 0`, the old INSERT supplies it explicitly, and the new code would simply stop writing it. D5's reason ("no field that is always false") is about the wire and UI, not the DB.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: rolling back to an older image after upgrading needs the telemetry DB removed, as with any release that adds a migration.

findings.title: Upgraders whose unconfigured apps use a shared base class lose them with no warning
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: a small user base (about 3 known users per project memory); the cost is a silently missing automation, which is hard to notice. Today autodetect imports modules and finds indirect subclasses (`class MyApp(BaseApp)`). After the change, an upgrader with no `[hassette.apps.*]` entries for those apps sees them stop running with no config error and no AST warning, and if some other apps are configured, the generic "No apps found" warning doesn't fire either. D1 accepts missed indirect subclasses for newcomers; the upgrader who relied on autodetect is a different population, and D1 doesn't examine them. The critic's heuristic alternative (scan for unresolved bases) contradicts the ratified "no base-class heuristics" scope and isn't offered.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: an upgrader whose unconfigured apps subclass a shared base class gets no warning when they stop loading.

findings.title: "Never raises" needs an explicit per-file guard, or one odd file takes startup down
findings.why_it_matters: Posture says the scan never raises and skips a file that "can't be read or parsed", wording that invites catching only `OSError`/`SyntaxError`. `ast.parse` can also raise `ValueError` (null bytes) or `RecursionError`/`MemoryError` (deeply nested source), `read_text()` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` on a non-UTF-8 file, and `rglob` raises from the iterator on an unreadable subdirectory. The scan is called in `startup_tasks` with no guard around it, so any of these takes down startup (a restart loop in Docker) for a log-only hint, against the design's own posture. One try/except around the whole scan would instead lose every class after the first bad file.
findings.recommended: A: In Posture's Failure-handling line, specify a per-file `except Exception` with a DEBUG log, parsing with `ast.parse(path.read_bytes())`, and a guard around the directory walk itself.
findings.chosen: A: In Posture's Failure-handling line, specify a per-file `except Exception` with a DEBUG log, parsing with `ast.parse(path.read_bytes())`, and a guard around the directory walk itself.

findings.title: An apps directory at a project root walks vendored trees and logs without a cap
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: users who point `apps.directory` at a project root or a directory with vendored trees. With `exclude_dirs` gone, the scan can't prune and the warning has no volume cap. `rglob("*.py")` walks into `node_modules`, `.tox`, `build`, `dist`, and virtualenvs not named `.venv`/`venv`, and only filters files afterward. Third-party `class Foo(App)` definitions then yield one WARNING with a snippet per class, and D7's only remedy is turning the warning off. The critic accepts the false positives themselves (ratified); the concern is the unpruned walk and unbounded output.
findings.recommended: C: Accept as a known limitation: an `apps.directory` pointed at a project root walks vendored trees and may log a warning per third-party `App` subclass.
findings.chosen: C: Accept as a known limitation: an `apps.directory` pointed at a project root walks vendored trees and may log a warning per third-party `App` subclass.

findings.title: Built-in exclusions match absolute path parts, so an apps directory under a `venv`/`.git`-named folder gets no warnings at all
findings.why_it_matters: The current exclusion test checks `exclude_dirs.intersection(full_path.parts)` against the resolved absolute path, not the parts relative to `apps.directory`. If the apps directory itself sits under a path component named `venv`, `.venv`, `.git`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, or `.mypy_cache`, every file is excluded and the scan silently finds nothing. D7 keeps the built-in exclusions "(renamed constant)", so reusing the existing check carries the quirk into the new scan.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: an apps directory under a folder named like a built-in exclusion never produces the warning.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: an apps directory under a folder named like a built-in exclusion never produces the warning.

findings.title: "Configured" comes from validated manifests, so a half-written entry gets two warnings
findings.why_it_matters: `clean_explicit_apps` skips entries missing `filename`/`class_name` and `remove_incomplete_apps` pops them, so a half-written entry never counts as configured. The user sees both "ignored: missing keys" and an unconfigured-class warning whose snippet duplicates their own entry's key. The behavior is consistent but noisy, and a half-written entry is a typical newcomer mistake. Correction to the critic's evidence: `AppManifest.validate_app_manifest` rewrites `app_dir` and `filename` when `app_dir` is a file, but not `full_path`, so the pre- and post-validation `full_path` values are the same. Matching on `manifest.full_path` is still the right key because it is the path the loader imports (`app_factory.py:191`, `app_utils.py:292`).
findings.chosen: Side A: Count only validated manifests
